clusters.title: The truth about dying: hospice workers on what loved ones should know
clusters.neutral_headline: The truth about dying: hospice workers on what loved ones should know

items.title: The truth about dying: hospice workers on what loved ones should know
items.standfirst: Anna Gordon met hospice care workers across the UK, learning how dignity and choice help create meaningful moments for patientsMost people in the UK actively avoid conversations about death and dying. They can be visibly uncomfortable when you raise the subject. When people try to talk about it, it tends to be euphemistically.This is a mistake, one that can stop you from making important choices for yourself or your loved ones. It can increase fear and misunderstanding about what death can look like, while open conversations can help to ease these feelings and bring a sense of calm, peace and, on occasion, even beauty to the event.Jenna Heritage: ‘Everyone’s big fear is that they are going to die in pain’ Continue reading...

items.title: Patients may miss out on NHS weight-loss jabs in England after GP funding withdrawn
items.standfirst: Inquiry finds most integrated care boards have scrapped payments to GPs for prescribing and monitoring the drugPatients who are eligible for potentially life-changing weight-loss injections on the NHS risk missing out after most integrated care boards (ICBs) in England withdrew funding for GP services, an investigation has found.The inquiry, conducted by the GP magazine Pulse, found that 21 of 36 ICBs have scrapped payments to practices for prescribing and monitoring Mounjaro, also known as tirzepatide. A further nine never had a local enhanced service and only four still retain one. Continue reading...

items.title: An album to keep your mind on track | Brief letters
items.standfirst: Steely Dan | Hot toddy | Dental advice | Christmas gifts | Black FridayI read with interest how Adrian Chiles traces his concentration challenges back to the CD shuffle button (Instant gratification is ruining our lives – and for me it started with my CD player’s shuffle button, 18 November). The simple solution is to play Aja by Steely Dan, in its glorious 39 minutes and 54 seconds’ entirety, and I promise you there will be absolutely no skipping or shuffling of tracks. Bren Pointer London• To mitigate the dental hygienist’s horror of a hot toddy (Letters, 20 November), how about having the hot water flavoured with sugar and lemon, followed by a swishing of the teeth with a generous helping of whisky?
